alternative: The ratio compares one passing sample from the edit with the median of up to three passing RL-Code samples. That setup puts the ratio near 1 for any single passing draw whose per-problem length distribution is close to RL-Code's. The edit is the base plus RL-Code's own top-8 directions at 1.5x, and it passes on about the same problems as RL-Code. Its answers are then just one more RL-Code-like draw, and the 1.5x size needs no further mechanism. A null that uses RL-Code against itself shows what such a draw gives: each passing RL seed's n_new divided by the median of the other seeds' passing n_new. The range [0.855, 1.035] holds that value as well. The geometric mean sits slightly below 1 because one draw is noisier than a median (a skewed log-length distribution against a pooled median), not because the edit changes how the model ends its answers.
computation: 1) Load the three RL-Code cells rlneurons/code1/rl_plain, rlneurons/xreward/code_hosts_s52/rl_plain and rlneurons/xreward/code_hosts_s53/rl_plain, one row per pid each. 2) For each seed i and each pid where seed i's row has passed true: take the n_new of the other two seeds' rows that passed. If there are none, skip the pid. Otherwise reference = their median (the mean of the two when both passed, the single value when one passed). Record ln(n_new_i / reference). 3) Pool the records over all three seeds and all pids. 4) Alternative value = exp(mean of the pooled logs), a unitless ratio on the statistic's scale.
